title: Ceuta Migration Surge & Schengen Crisis Tracker Update — Fri Sep 18, 2026
summary: The European Parliament passed a non-binding resolution Sep 17 (339-225-16) backing Spanish sovereignty over Ceuta and describing the July crossing as 'hybrid warfare,' though Morocco's EU/NATO ambassador said it carries no condemnation of Rabat. On Sep 18, police transferred over 3,000 migrants from beach camps to a new Poniente port reception site built for only 1,700, prompting officials to roughly double their estimate of migrants remaining in Ceuta to 9,000-10,000. A Moroccan man was arrested trying to smuggle two migrants onto the Algeciras ferry, and Spain's national football team filmed its Nations League squad announcement in Ceuta as a solidarity gesture.

title: Ceuta / Schengen Crisis Update — Sep 6, 2026
summary: Spain's Transport Ministry authorised the temporary occupation of 16,000 m² of Ceuta's port to house over 1,000 migrants in tents, overriding a vote by the Port Authority's own board against the installation. The move follows a Sept 2 written denial from National Police Director General Francisco Pardo to Interior Minister Grande-Marlaska that any police report attributes the July 30-31 crossing to Moroccan security forces — contradicting the CENIF document that surfaced Sept 1 — which itself came after nationwide Ceuta solidarity protests (roughly 50,000 in Madrid) ended in a far-right-led riot outside Congress, with tear gas, rubber bullets, four arrests and RTVE journalists assaulted in Madrid, Ceuta and Barcelona. Separately, Interior Ministry data show Ceuta's land arrivals more than doubled in 2026 even excluding the July surge, and Brussels confirmed it will send a technical mission to Ceuta after a Marlaska-Brunner call citing 'important progress' on EU support. The official death toll cited by PM Sánchez in his Sept 3 Congress address rose to 141, up from the previously confirmed 111.

title: Ceuta / Schengen Crisis Update — Sep 2, 2026
summary: Spain's Council of Ministers approved a €309 million emergency decree-law (plus €50M in loan guarantees) for Ceuta's security, minors' care, businesses and services, alongside confirmation that reception capacity has more than doubled to over 3,400 places within a week. National Police intelligence told the investigating judge that Moroccan gendarmes and plainclothes agents actively guided the July 30-31 crossing, prompting a three-hour meeting between King Felipe VI and PM Sánchez ahead of a fresh Security Council session. A government analysis found relocating Ceuta's roughly 2,678 migrant minors would take nearly four years at the current transfer pace. On Sept 2, PP leader Feijóo led nationwide Ceuta solidarity protests overshadowing the city's local holiday, after Madrid's government delegation denied a permit for the Madrid rally he and Vox's Abascal attended anyway — a day before Sánchez's Sept 3 Congress appearance.

title: Ceuta / Schengen Crisis Update — Aug 30, 2026
summary: One month after the mass crossing, Spain's Council of Ministers approved a €165 million emergency economic package for Ceuta (€80M near-term, €70M for 2027, plus a separate €180M medium-term plan), and Secretary of State for Security Aina Calvo relocated to the city to directly oversee accommodation and returns under a command now chaired by PM Sánchez, with a two-week target to clear the streets. Reports emerged of Muslim residents being targeted by protesters for helping migrants, raising fears of a religious divide in a city historically split roughly 45% Muslim/55% Christian. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo made Ceuta the centerpiece of the political season's opening, organizing nationwide Sept 2 protests ahead of Sánchez's planned Sept 3 Congress appearance. A backfilled Aug 24 event covers Spain's earlier €32M EU emergency migration fund request, and a new media retrospective (The Olive Press) put the crossing's death toll above 150 — the highest figure reported to date, now flagged as a heavily contested estimate alongside the 111 official and 141 NGO tallies.

title: Ceuta / Schengen Crisis Update — Aug 27, 2026
summary: The crisis's first violent clashes erupted after a demonstration late Wednesday drew thousands of residents; police fired tear gas to keep them from migrants camped on the beach. Early Thursday, roughly 70 migrants ambushed and stoned a military vehicle carrying four soldiers in Benzú, injuring one and prompting 12 arrests. Hours later, residents blocked a Red Cross food truck for over two hours before breaking a police cordon at Benítez beach, storming the migrant camp and setting fire to shelters. Ceuta's finance councillor Kissy Chandiramani said tension in the city is 'very high' amid 'no response' from Madrid, while the national government approved a 'single command' under Minister Ángel Víctor Torres to coordinate five ministries and an extra €25M for unaccompanied minors' care. Torres said return to Morocco remains the priority but will be a long process.

title: Ceuta / Schengen Crisis Update — Aug 26, 2026
summary: Spain's Interior Ministry revised its count of unaccompanied migrant minors in Ceuta down from 2,168 to roughly 1,500 after a database audit found duplicate case entries. PM Pedro Sánchez convened an extraordinary National Security Council meeting on Aug 24, with officials acknowledging the city remains 'very far' from normality; former EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell separately called the wider European response 'hysterical, disproportionate and absurd.' Madrid announced plans to reform Spain's asylum law to align with the EU's Migration and Asylum Pact. Spain's anti-racism observatory (OBERAXE) reported nearly 9,600 hate posts tied to the crisis logged in just two days, part of a broader jump in hate-speech content in July. The El Trampolín beach camp was fully rebuilt within a day of the Aug 21 eviction attempt, prompting the city to suspend beach-cleaning operations.

title: Ceuta / Schengen Crisis Update — Aug 24, 2026
summary: Roughly 500 migrants who were relocated from Ceuta's El Trampolín beach camp on Aug 20 returned within hours and rebuilt a makeshift camp, forcing authorities to attempt a second eviction on Aug 21. Ceuta president Juan Vivas said moving people between locations in the city 'does not show a willingness to solve the problem,' and the city government warned it would suspend beach-cleaning operations if the cycle continued, citing crew safety. Migration Minister Elma Saiz said the government aims to expand reception capacity to roughly 4,000 places via four additional humanitarian sites. The Italy-Spain reciprocal Schengen border checks remain unchanged, still set to run to Sep 1 (Italy) and Sep 7 (Spain).

title: Ceuta / Schengen Crisis Update — Aug 23, 2026
summary: Spanish police began clearing the makeshift El Trampolín beach camp on Aug 20, relocating over 1,200 of roughly 4,000 migrants to two new temporary shelters, Loma Margarita and El Embolsamiento. Human Rights Watch said on Aug 21 that Spain must urgently fix a 'humanitarian and rights crisis' after thousands spent nearly three weeks without adequate shelter or sanitation. Moroccan forces dispersed a 294-person regrouping attempt near Fnideq on Aug 16, the first sizeable new crossing bid since the July 30-31 surge. Spain is separately preparing a mainland transfer of roughly 500 unaccompanied migrant girls over EU objections, after several Spanish autonomous communities refused to accept minors from the crisis, and the EU announced it will boost Morocco border-control funding by an additional €190 million through 2027 as part of a pending partnership deal.
